svg.text: Figure 1a — Runtime Architecture and Threat Overview
Juice Shop · 8 components · 21 data flows · 11 trust boundaries · 72 threats in the model

g.data-boundary-ids: tb-1 tb-2 tb-3 tb-4 tb-6 tb-7 tb-11 tb-12
g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 External → C-04; tb-2 External → C-03; tb-3 External → C-04; tb-4 External → C-06; tb-6 External → C-06; tb-7 External → C-02; tb-11 C-04 → External; tb-12 C-02 → External
Trust boundary crossing: tb-8 C-04 → C-09; tb-9 C-08 → C-07
df-001: Server fetches requester-supplied profile image URL (HTTP)
df-002: POST of challenge solution, CTF flag and host info to configured webhook (HTTP)
df-003: NFTMinted contract event subscription over WebSocket RPC using ALCHEMY_API_KEY (WebSocket) df-004: ContractExploited event subscription over WebSocket RPC (WebSocket)
df-005: Chatbot requests to configured OpenAI-compatible LLM with API key (HTTP)

df-006: Login with email and password (HTTP) df-006 authentication: Login handler checks email and hashed password against the Users table; TOTP token required if a secret is set; evidence: routes/login.ts:34
df-007: Socket.IO events (challenge notifications) with CORS origin localhost:4200 (WebSocket)

df-008: Sequelize queries against embedded SQLite (SQLite) df-008 authentication: Embedded SQLite engine inside the application process; the engine has no login of its own.; evidence: models/index.ts:34

df-009: Reviews and orders collections in embedded MarsDB (MarsDB) df-009 authentication: Embedded MarsDB engine inside the application process; the engine has no login of its own.; evidence: data/mongodb.ts:9, data/mongodb.ts:10

df-011: OAuth authorization (HTTPS) df-011 authentication: The identity provider authenticates the user at its sign-in endpoint; evidence: frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:31, frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:148
df-012: OAuth profile request (HTTPS) df-012 authentication: The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request; evidence: frontend/src/app/Services/user.service.ts:68

df-014: API requests (bearer) (HTTP) df-014 authentication: the handler checks a bearer credential and rejects the request without it; evidence: lib/insecurity.ts:178, lib/insecurity.ts:52, routes/orderHistory.ts:13, lib/insecurity.ts:156
df-015: API requests (unknown authentication) (HTTP) df-016: API requests (unknown authentication) (HTTP)

df-017: API requests (bearer) (HTTP) df-018: API requests (other) (HTTP) df-017 authentication: the handler checks a bearer credential and rejects the request without it; evidence: lib/insecurity.ts:178, lib/insecurity.ts:52 df-017 access group: API access; alternatives; step n/a df-018 authentication: the handler checks the supplied TOTP code against the account secret and rejects an invalid code; evidence: routes/2fa.ts:31 df-018 access group: API access; alternatives; step n/a

df-020: Direct requests (cookie) (HTTP) df-020 authentication: the handler checks a cookie credential and rejects the request without it; evidence: routes/profileImageFileUpload.ts:35, routes/profileImageUrlUpload.ts:21, routes/userProfile.ts:34, routes/updateUserProfile.ts:17, routes/dataErasure.ts:26, routes/dataErasure.ts:76
Internet Attacker → C-04 · Juice Shop Express Server: scenario 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6; its findings also affect C-06 · Authentication & Session Surface
Internet Attacker → C-06 · Authentication & Session Surface: scenario 1, 2, 4, 5; its findings also affect C-08 · Sequelize application data access
Internet Attacker → C-02 · Web3 / Wallet / NFT Surface: scenario 5; its findings also affect C-06 · Authentication & Session Surface
Internet Attacker → Juice Shop User: scenario 6
Dynamic code evaluation — evidence: lib/xml.ts:12, lib/xml.ts:38, routes/b2bOrder.ts:23, routes/captcha.ts:22

Further capabilities: WebSocket endpoint — evidence: lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:20, lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:23; Blockchain client — evidence: routes/nftMint.ts:18, routes/web3Wallet.ts:20
C-04 · Juice Shop Express Server: CTF flags and solution data
C-06 · Authentication & Session Surface: JWT session tokens
C-09 · MarsDB Store: Product reviews and orders
Arbitrary host chosen by the requester via imageUrl; fetched by the server.
HTTP endpoint selected by the SOLUTIONS_WEBHOOK setting, notified when a challenge is solved.
Blockchain RPC endpoint reached over WebSocket for contract event listening.
OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint whose base URL comes from application.chatBot.llmApiUrl config.
Person using the client application, evidenced by its browser entry point.
OAuth authorization: https://accounts.google.com. Activation depends on deployment configuration.
Trust change inside this column: tb-10 C-05 → External

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
trust change within a column (dashed: inferred)
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE category: filled = findings in that category
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
finding; +N = further labels, listed under Further capabilities.
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
Stored username runs as server code
The recipient performs no authentication check on this connection.
The recipient checks the supplied password.
The recipient checks the token supplied with the request.
A session cookie identifies the caller.
Delegated access; only the evidenced protocol step is covered.
the handler checks the supplied TOTP code against the account
secret and rejects an invalid code
Authentication could not be determined from the code.
Numbered hexagon: authentication · circle: attack scenario
Red: absent / unsafe · yellow: standard / limited · green: stronger
Method properties, not proof of a secure implementation.
